discoveries.title: The index is not a strike-rate list
discoveries.body: IPL batting correlation with career strike rate is 0.05. The top 10 shares 3 names with the best career strike rates.

discoveries.title: Bowling order did not repeat
discoveries.body: 2026 holdout, players with 25 pressure and 25 baseline balls on each side: bowling sign agreement 49% and rank correlation 0.11 (51 bowlers). Batting sign agreement 81%, rank correlation 0.32.

discoveries.title: Collapse overs move the extreme names
discoveries.body: Chase-only gaps keep rank correlation 0.90 for batters, and only 4 of the batting top 10.

discoveries.title: A high index is not a Royals requirement
discoveries.body: IPL bowling correlation with the unadjusted pressure gap is 0.96. The war room still refuses the IPL bowling rank leader because his T20I pressure gap reverses and opening is not the squad hole.

requirements.title: Spin under pressure
requirements.detail: Bishnoi pressure economy 10.1 versus baseline 8.2 on 309 balls. Fifth percentile -2.46. Jadeja middle-overs economy 7.7 on 1177 balls, with a negative bowling pressure gap.

requirements.title: Later-order batting
requirements.detail: Hetmyer is the directory batter in the strict set at median order 6, index 75.4. Jurel index 58.9 and Parag index 61.0 have intervals that cross below zero. Dubey has 90 pressure and 53 baseline balls.

requirements.title: Death pace at volume
requirements.detail: Sandeep death economy 10.7 on 343 balls. Deshpande 11.1 on 341. Archer pressure economy 7.2 but death economy 10.4 on 225. Burger death economy 7.5 on 69 balls.

requirements.title: Opening is not the buying need
requirements.detail: Jaiswal baseline strike rate 155 on 1477 balls and 8 pressure balls. Sooryavanshi baseline strike rate 229 on 449 balls and 0 pressure balls.

scenarios.condition: 2026 directory core is still at the franchise when the register opens. This is not known.
scenarios.first_action: One pressure spinner, Yuzvendra Chahal if he is in the pool.
scenarios.second_action: One later-order batter, Rinku Singh if he is in the pool.
scenarios.not_doing: No opener. No second spinner. No bid ordered by raw bowling PPI.

scenarios.condition: One acquisition. No 2027 purse balance is published, so this is a role choice, not a price.
scenarios.first_action: The spinner. Hetmyer and Jadeja already clear the strict batting rule. Bishnoi's bowling interval does not.
scenarios.second_action: If that spinner is not registered, the one buy is Rinku Singh.
scenarios.not_doing: Do not spend the single slot on Tim David, Naman Dhir, or a death bowler.

scenarios.condition: Rinku Singh is not in the auction pool.
scenarios.first_action: Jitesh Sharma, then Tim David, then Naman Dhir.
scenarios.second_action: The spinner remains the other slot in the ideal case.
scenarios.not_doing: Do not replace them with Shreyas Iyer or Sanju Samson. David Miller stays off this chain because his T20I gap reverses.

scenarios.condition: Yuzvendra Chahal is not in the auction pool.
scenarios.first_action: Leave the spin hole open rather than auto-bid for Maheesh Theekshana.
scenarios.second_action: Theekshana is the watchlist name, with a negative T20I gap and no 2026 IPL appearance in this pack.
scenarios.not_doing: Do not move Jadeja's strong middle-overs economy into a claim that the pressure gap is solved.

scenarios.condition: Only if the high-volume death options on the directory are released. That list does not exist.
scenarios.first_action: No death bowler is in the top 5. The class failed the 2026 sign check.
scenarios.second_action: Watchlist order for that role starts with the contradiction stated: Avesh Khan has the best IPL interval and a worse T20I pressure economy.
scenarios.not_doing: Do not treat Jofra Archer's positive pressure gap as death-over control. His IPL death economy is 10.4 on 225 balls.

sources.statement: Franchise squad page lists 25 players under the heading Rajasthan Royals Squad 2026, grouped as wicket-keepers, batters, all-rounders, and bowlers. It includes Dasun Shanaka and Emanjot and does not list Sam Curran or Kuldeep Sen.

IPL media advisory of 15 November 2025: RR retained 16 players for IPL 2026, 7 marked overseas, total spent Rs 108.95 crore, salary cap remaining Rs 16.05 crore. Names: Dhruv Jurel, Donovan Ferreira (T), Jofra Archer, Kwena Maphaka, Lhuan-Dre Pretorious, Nandre Burger, Ravindra Jadeja (T), Riyan Parag, Sam Curran (T), Sandeep Sharma, Shimron Hetmyer, Shubham Dubey, Tushar Deshpande, Vaibhav Suryavanshi, Yashaswi Jaiswal, Yudhvir Charak. Asterisk in the source marks overseas; (T) marks a traded player. This is the 2026 retention, not the 2027 retention.

Franchise article dated 15 November 2025 lists 13 retained players and names trades for Ravindra Jadeja, Sam Curran, and Donovan Ferreira. Spellings on this page: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Yudhvir Singh, Lhuan-dre Pretorius.

Franchise article dated 16 December 2025: nine auction buys totalling Rs 13.40 crore, forming a 25-man IPL 2026 squad. Ravi Bishnoi Rs 7.20 crore; Adam Milne Rs 2.40 crore; Ravi Singh Rs 95 lakh; Sushant Mishra Rs 90 lakh; Kuldeep Sen Rs 75 lakh; Vignesh Puthur, Yash Raj Punja, Brijesh Sharma, and Aman Rao Perala Rs 30 lakh each. Article states Bishnoi has represented India and calls Milne a New Zealand pacer.
Franchise article dated 23 March 2026: Dasun Shanaka named as the IPL 2026 replacement for injured Sam Curran. Fee not stated on this page. Shanaka described as a Sri Lankan all-rounder.

IPL media advisory dated 23 May 2026: Emanjot Chahal signed as replacement for Ravi Singh, ruled out of the rest of IPL 2026 with a hamstring injury, fee INR 30 lakh. Described as a young all-rounder from Patiala.

Kuldeep Sen was an auction purchase in the 16 December 2025 franchise article and is absent from the squad directory fetched on 2026-11-14. No official release notice was found in this pass. 2026 end-of-season status and 2027 availability are unresolved.

No official Rajasthan Royals or IPL page published an IPL 2027 retained or released list. The retention deadline had not passed on the access date. Unofficial predicted lists were found and were not loaded.

IPL Governing Council media advisory, 28 September 2024: total salary cap is Rs 146 crore (2025), Rs 151 crore (2026), and Rs 157 crore (2027). The cap consists of auction purse, incremental performance pay, and match fees. It is not a pure auction purse. The same advisory sets the auction purse at INR 120 crore for IPL 2025 only.

Same 28 September 2024 advisory: each playing member, including the Impact Player, receives a match fee of INR 7.5 lakh per match in addition to the contracted amount. Impact Player regulation continues for the 2025 to 2027 cycle.

The same advisory's limit of 6 retentions or RTMs, with at most 5 capped players and 2 uncapped players, is the mega-auction rule written for entry into the 2025-27 cycle. It is not restated there as the 2027 mini-auction retention cap, and it is not applied in this project as a 2027 rule.

Same advisory: an Indian player becomes uncapped if, in the five calendar years before the season, he has not played in the starting XI in a Test, ODI, or T20I and does not hold a BCCI central contract. Overseas registration rules in that advisory refer to the big auction.

ESPNcricinfo, 2 November 2026: IPL told franchises the 2027 retention deadline moved from 15 November to 17 November 2026; player registration closes 23 November; additional requests until 27 November; final auction register and sets on 3 December; mini-auction on 16 December 2026 in Goa. Described as the last mini-auction of the cycle, with a mega auction ahead of 2028. No matching IPL.com media advisory was found.

Same ESPNcricinfo article: IPL 2027 dates are not finalised. A March 14 to May 30 window was set out in 2024, and the board secretary later indicated a start around the end of March. Start date is not confirmed.

Fan and news pages published predicted RR retentions and releases for 2027, including prices. Those pages label themselves as prediction, rumour, or pre-deadline speculation. None are loaded as squad facts.

Spellings differ across official pages and this dataset. Dataset and RR site use Yashasvi Jaiswal, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Yudhvir Singh, Lhuan Pretorius or Lhuan-dre Pretorius. IPL retention advisory uses Yashaswi Jaiswal, Vaibhav Suryavanshi, Yudhvir Charak, Lhuan-Dre Pretorious. Auction article uses Yash Raj Punja; dataset name is Yash Punja. Squad page uses Emanjot; IPL advisory uses Emanjot Chahal; dataset name is Emanjot Singh Chahal. Each pair is one player_id in this dataset, recorded here rather than merged by a fuzzy name join.
sources.publisher: Indian Premier League and Rajasthan Royals

sources.statement: News coverage has quoted a possible purse change from Rs 125 crore to Rs 150 crore and a secretary's denial of that change, while also saying 16 December 2026 is not a mega auction. Those purse numbers are not the figures on the IPL advisory, which states a Rs 120 crore auction purse for 2025 and a Rs 157 crore total salary cap for 2027. The 125/150 pair is not used as a rule. The NDTV article was not re-fetched in full.
ESPNcricinfo reported a Shanaka replacement fee of INR 2 crore. The franchise announcement that was fetched does not state a fee. The fee is not treated as confirmed.
